```{=html}
    <h1>The cosmological constant</h1>
  </header>
```

::: {.qft-exam-body}
- Show that a nonzero (infinite!) vacuum energy density of a quantum field redefines the cosmological constant in Einstein's equations.

- Discuss how the solution describing the evolution of a homogeneous and isotropic Universe changes depending on the contributions of fermion and boson fields to the vacuum energy.

- Study the literature on modern experimental measurements of the cosmological constant in the model of a homogeneous and isotropic Universe. State what properties a system must have to explain the observed accelerated expansion of the Universe.

- Consider the simplest supersymmetric model, the Wess--Zumino model [\[1\]](#ref-1), which contains one complex scalar $\phi$ and one Majorana fermion $\psi$. Obtain the mean vacuum energy density. Does supersymmetry solve the cosmological constant problem?

## References

[1]{#ref-1} Wess, Julius, Zumino, Bruno, *Supergauge transformations in four dimensions*, Nucl. Phys. B **70** 39–50 (1974) <https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(74)90355-1>

:::
